subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: What pace/admission surface should OpenClaw core own for autonomous agents?
rationale: The request adds public config, provider usage state, status and tool API contracts, persistence, and autonomous throttling behavior; automation cannot safely choose those defaults or ownership boundaries.

options.title: Visibility First
options.body: Expose provider windows and projected pace in `openclaw status` and `session_status`, but defer automatic blocking until semantics are proven.

options.title: Opt-In Admission
options.body: Add `agents.defaults.pace` with explicit subagent/noninteractive gates, durable state, and tests for both compatibility defaults and opt-in throttling.

options.title: Plugin/API Boundary
options.body: Keep automatic pacing outside core for now and only extend missing provider usage and agent-facing status APIs.

recommendation.title: Visibility First
recommendation.body: Expose provider windows and projected pace in `openclaw status` and `session_status`, but defer automatic blocking until semantics are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available product/API scoping signal for the provider transport and security-sensitive egress boundary this feature would touch.
